notes: expectedPages are PDF page indices (1-12). expectedAnswerContains strings are matched against the answer after normalizing case, whitespace and thousands separators. valueStrings (optional, default = expectedAnswerContains) are the strings that must ALL appear in ONE retrieved chunk for a 'value hit'. kind is the element the answer lives in (chart/table/callout/footnote/paragraph). out-of-scope items expect exactly the refusal string.

items.question: How much less energy does iMac use compared to the ENERGY STAR requirement?
items.note: p7 lead line and the ENERGY STAR paragraph both say 'iMac uses/consumes 58 percent less energy than the requirement for ENERGY STAR' (marker 18). Plain prose, not a chart.

items.question: What is the total carbon footprint of the iMac, and how much comes from product use versus manufacturing?
items.note: p10 table 1 (iMac two ports 256GB): total 346 kg CO2e; Production 50%, Transportation 5%, Product use 45%, End-of-life <1%. 'Manufacturing' = the table's 'Production' row. Four-port 512GB (391 kg) is a different column; the chunk must keep the two-port header with the rows. The bare strings '50'/'45' in the correctness check are weak (any 50 or 45 passes); judge by hand if in doubt.

items.question: What material is the iMac stand made from, and what percentage of it is recycled?
valueStrings: 100 percent recycled aluminum in the stand
items.note: p1 banner 'iMac uses 100% recycled aluminum in the stand' (written with a % sign, so the p1 chunk will not match the 'percent' valueString; p4 callout and p2 paragraph use 'percent'). Overall device recycled content (more than 15 percent) is a different number and a possible distractor.

items.question: In the progress toward carbon neutral chart, what are the baseline emissions, the emissions reductions, and the resulting iMac emissions?
items.note: p2 stacked-bar chart (vector, no raster): 445 kg baseline, -99 kg reductions (written with an en dash), 346 kg iMac emissions; 445 - 99 = 346. The answer lives only in the chart labels; the chart has no per-segment numbers. Value hit needs all three labels in one chunk (plain text puts '445 kg' ~30 lines away from '346 kg').

items.question: What is the carbon footprint of the four-port, 512GB iMac?
items.note: p10 table 2: 'iMac (four ports) 512GB 391 kg CO2e'. Trap: the 346 kg figure is the two-port 256GB. Only in the table.

items.question: How much power does the iMac draw in Idle (display on) at 115V?
items.note: p12 'Power consumption for iMac' table: Idle-Display On 20.5W (100V), 20.6W (115V), 20.9W (230V). Values are row-wise in the text but the 100V/115V/230V headers are separated, so a chunk containing 20.6W does not prove the voltage is known; the value hit cannot test that and is therefore generous here. Check the answer by hand for 115V vs 100V/230V confusion.

items.question: What is the power adapter efficiency at 230V?
items.note: p12 table: Power adapter efficiency 91.1% (100V), 91.5% (115V), 91.9% (230V). Same header-separation caveat as g06.

items.question: How much of the iMac packaging is recycled content?
items.note: p6 paragraph 'Our packaging for iMac contains 76 percent recycled content' and the big-number callout '76%'. Distractors: 100% fiber-based, 100% responsibly sourced virgin wood fiber, more than 15 percent device recycled content.

items.question: Does the 100 percent recycled copper in the thermal module components apply to every iMac model?
items.note: p4 Copper callout cites footnote 14 (p11): 'Recycled copper in the thermal module applies to iMac (four ports) only.' The callout alone reads as unconditional; the caveat is only in the footnote. Value hit needs the footnote text appended to (or retrieved in) the same chunk as 'thermal module' (D-08). Correct answer is 'No, four ports only'; the 'four ports' string check cannot detect a wrong 'yes' that also mentions it, judge failures by hand.

items.question: Which iMac configuration (ports and storage) does the 346 kg carbon footprint figure apply to?
items.note: DOCUMENT CONTRADICTS ITSELF. p10 table and the p2 paragraph say iMac (two ports) 256GB = 346 kg (four ports 512GB = 391 kg). p2 footnote 10 (printed on p11) says the LCA is 'based on iMac (two ports) with 512GB storage configuration'. Decision: follow the p10 table (256GB). An answer of '512GB' fails; an answer that also flags the footnote conflict is acceptable but is not checked automatically. Value hit uses p10/p2 (the p11 footnote cannot satisfy it). Flag to user.

items.question: How many hours of battery life does the iMac have?
items.note: Not in the document. Verified: pdftotext over all 12 pages; 'battery' appears only in 'modeling daily battery drain' (p9, use-phase method) and cobalt in Apple-designed batteries (p4, p11 fn 13). No battery life figure.

items.question: How much does the iMac weigh?
items.note: Not in the document. Verified: no 'weigh', pounds, lb or product-mass figure in pdftotext of all 12 pages; the only 'weight' mentions are 'packaging by weight' (p1/p11 fn 3). Mild risk: the model might answer with a packaging figure; that would be a real refusal failure.
